title: transactions distributed consistency saga outbox and inbox
concepts: A local database transaction can make a set of changes atomic within its supported transaction boundary; it does not automatically include an HTTP service, message broker, or another service's database.

A dual write that updates business data and publishes a message as separate operations can lose or duplicate one side when a process crashes. The transactional outbox writes business state and an outgoing message record in the same local transaction, then relays it asynchronously.

The outbox relay can publish more than once if it crashes after publishing but before recording progress, so downstream consumers still need idempotency or inbox deduplication. Outbox and inbox patterns reduce specific failure windows; they do not create one global exactly-once transaction.

A saga coordinates a business operation as a sequence of local transactions. Choreography lets participants react to messages; orchestration uses a coordinator that tracks progress and commands participants. Both need explicit retry, timeout, idempotency, and recovery rules.

Compensation is a new business action that semantically counteracts a committed step; it is not a database rollback and may not restore the exact prior state. Compensating steps can fail, encounter concurrent changes, require a different order, or need human intervention.

Choose local ACID transactions, distributed commit, saga, outbox, and inbox from the consistency requirement and supported resource boundaries. Prefer simpler local transactions when one store can own the invariant; make temporary inconsistency and recovery observable when coordination is unavoidable.

versionNotes.edition: Azure Cosmos DB Transactional Outbox sample, updated July 2026
items: The current Cosmos DB sample uses a transactional batch for business state plus event records and a change feed relay. Its atomicity is bounded to a supported logical partition and its change-feed delivery remains at-least-once, so consumers deduplicate by event ID.

scopeExclusions: CQRS and event sourcing as distinct architecture choices (t08-005)
Broker queues, offsets, delivery attempts, and product-specific guarantees (t08-008)
Generic retry, circuit breaker, backoff, idempotency-key, and rate-limiter implementations (t08-009)
SQL Server and EF Core transaction APIs, savepoints, execution strategies, and provider limitations (tracks 03 and 04)
Compensating actions are not exact inverses or global database rollback, and saga/outbox/inbox do not claim arbitrary end-to-end exactly-once execution
Two-phase commit is included for comparison and is not presented as categorically unavailable; suitability depends on participant support and operational requirements
